_what: The town's stamp-related dials, in the open. Sister of the World's dials block (postmark-world WORLD/world-state.json). The money law's numbers live here — readable by residents and machines alike, not buried in code.
_classes: read_side dials tune derived displays and may change freely (prospective, no replay impact). law_side dials bind the verifier: changes are prospective only and era-dated — history stays lawful under the rules of its day (the ballot's frozen-rules precedent).

weight._note: mark weight = sum of open escrows + k x unique staking households OTHER THAN the mark's own. Breadth term per the 2026-07-28 ruling (ECONOMY 9.2's determination kernel: linear plus per-unique-household, never quadratic in hierarchical contexts).
weight._external_only: 2026-08-05, Keemin-ruled: k is the breadth term and a household wanting its own mark is not breadth. Measured the day it changed: of 12 marks carrying escrow, 11 drew k from their own household and 10 of those had no external backing at all — so the whale-resistance term was mostly paying authors for caring about their own work. Self-staking remains free and allowed (law_side below is unchanged): own stamps still count in full toward raw escrow, still anchor the mark against retirement, still show in the staker's portfolio. Only the bonus is withheld. Read-side, so prospective and replay-neutral — the sealed ledger is untouched and no historical entry changes meaning; derived weight moves at the next Settlement.

town_issuance._what: The town minting into its own treasury: `MINT -> <treasury> · <n> · for: issuance:<purpose> · by: <who> · note: <provenance>`. NOT a founder gift — a gift lands on a resident and the mint refuses a handle with no WHITE_PAGES room, and the treasury has no room because the town is not a resident. This class keeps the gift strict and pays for its own looseness with laws a gift does not carry: the recipient must be the handle declared here, and every line must name a purpose and carry a provenance note.
town_issuance._mint_at_demand: Keemin-ruled 2026-08-10: the treasury has NO operating float. Resting state is zero — it spends income first and mints only the shortfall, and every mint line carries its purpose. So issuance REPEATS by design and the class is a series, not a one-off. That is why uniqueness is narrow: only `once_purposes` are one-shot, since a blanket one-per-purpose rule would forbid minting twice for the same recurring need.
town_issuance._once_purposes: Purposes that may appear at most once, ever. Enforced at the door AND in the verifier's lawful fold, so a second line slipped in by any route fails to verify. `founding-grant` is here because a founding act happens once; a later era declares its own slug rather than needing a code change. If this dial is unreadable the verifier SKIPS the check and says so in its notes rather than passing silently.
town_issuance._treasury_is_not_a_resident: `the-town` holds no stamps and has no WHITE_PAGES room as of 2026-08-10. That is why issuance must precede the founding stakes rather than merely being first in a tidy order: stakes clip to the staker's liquid balance, so without it every stake applies 0 with a reason rather than failing loudly.
town_issuance._declared_not_exercised: Written 2026-08-10 as part of the founding-act build. No issuance line exists in the ledger. Declaring the dial does not authorize the act; the act is Keemin's word.

world_stake._ruled: 2026-07-28 P3 build-gate; ECONOMY.md stake-subset ratified by Keemin by name (breadth, not caps, is the whale-resistance).

keeping._rho_owner: R10 (Keemin, 2026-08-21 mid-morning): 'rho = 0.5 at launch — at the constitutional ceiling, superseding the sitting's 0.25. The dial opens with no upward headroom (the first ballot may only lower it) and the genesis floor becomes operative: holo may drain the founder's line the full way to half of parity.' THIS FIELD IS THE OWNER OF THE NUMBER — 'every other surface reads it rather than restating it'. A doc, a page or a comment that restates 0.5 has forked the dial; write the mechanism instead ('rho, from the keeping dial') and let the reader look here. RE-AIMED 2026-09-14: with holo retired for pots, rho caps the FUNDING MINT — a household's fresh mint from one close ≤ rho × its earned base. RE-BASED 2026-09-17 at the founder's ruling: that base is the household's ALL-SOURCES mint before the close, primary AND holo — 'funding minted stamps contribute to the max stamps you can get from another fund. it compounds by design.' The number and the constitutional ceiling are unchanged, but note what moved: R10's genesis floor ('holo may drain the founder's line the full way to half of parity') assumed a base that money could not raise. Under a PER-CLOSE cap over a base each close enlarges, nothing in this dial bounded the compound — flagged to the founder on #2811 (POS-33) rather than decided by the lane that built the close. RE-SHAPED 2026-09-17 at the founder's answer to that flag, verbatim: 'ceiling cap is fine.' So rho caps HOLDINGS, not one close's mint: a household's holo AFTER a close is capped at rho × its all-sources mint BEFORE it, and the close mints at most max(0, floor(rho × base) − the holo the household already holds). The base still compounds by design; the ceiling is what bounds it. At rho = 0.5 the iteration converges on holo ≤ primary per household — R10's genesis floor restored as arithmetic, and the constitution's own sentence ('money can come to own up to half of Postmark; it can never own more') stated one household at a time.
keeping._what: The funding seam's epoch-close arithmetic (keeping pots — grammar: stamp-mint.mjs § THE FUNDING SEAM; tool: tools/epoch-close.mjs, manual founder-run). AMENDED 2026-09-14 at the founder's ruling, and again 2026-09-17 in two steps — the rho base re-based to the all-sources mint at 04:2x ('it compounds by design'), and the cap itself re-shaped from one close's mint to the household's HOLDINGS at 09:0x ('ceiling cap is fine'): at close, the funded fraction is min(1, non-treasury dollars / the pot's posted target_usd_per_epoch) — an elastic pot reads 1 once its roll has met its floor; EVERY OPEN STAKE RETURNS WHOLE (pot-return rows); the funding mint M = floor(fraction × the open staked mass) is minted as holo rows to the payers, one per receipt, by dollar share of the roll, a payer's own household's stakes excluded from the mass sized for that payer, floors per payer, the remainder un-minted; and a household's holo after the close is capped at rho × its all-sources mint before it — money's share of a household may never pass rho. The base is primary and holo and it compounds by design (04:2x); the CAP is on holdings, not on one close's mint (09:0x, 'ceiling cap is fine'), so a close mints a household at most the room left: max(0, floor(rho × base) − the holo it already holds). Nothing burns. The pre-amendment arithmetic (the funded share of each stake burned; σ of a staker's burn minted back as keeping mint with no liquid coin; (1−σ)·B as holo to the payers) stands in this file's history and in the PSAs of 2026-08-21/23; no close ever ran under it. The rule in one breath: A stake on a pot is weight lent, as it is everywhere else in town: it comes home whole at the close. What the stakes do is size the reward. At a close, the mass they lent, scaled by how funded the pot was, is minted to the givers as holo rows — one per receipt, and liquid like any stamp — by dollar share of the roll, own household excluded, floors per giver, remainder un-minted, and no household's holo AFTER the close passes rho × its all-sources mint BEFORE it — money's share of a household may never pass rho. Nothing burns; the keeping record retires.
keeping._no_rate: There is NO dollar-to-stamp exchange rate anywhere in this system, and the funded fraction is why. Dollars are priced against the town's own POSTED NEED, never against the staked mass, so a fully funded pot lends its whole staked mass to the givers' mint however large the pile and an unfunded one mints nothing. That is the design's point: the community itself prices how much reward a dollar earns, by what it chooses to stake. The pot never says what a stamp is worth in dollars; the stakers say how much the givers deserve.
keeping._holo: AMENDED 2026-09-17 at the founder's ruling ("non-spendable is repealed; the stamps are like any other, but are holo to signify the special source"): the givers' reward IS the holo row — one per receipt the close settles, `<n>` may be 0 (the receipt's one mint chance spent) — and holo stamps are LIQUID: they count in the payer's balance and in minted-cumulative and they stake, vote, pay and transfer like any stamp. "Holo" names the source, not a restriction; the town shows them in holo ink. The arrow-free shape stays (a holo row is a mint, not a movement); the balance and mint folds credit it by kind. The 2026-09-14 line this replaces — "RETIRED for the funding seam … ordinary fresh mint, liquid, source-tagged `for: funding:<pot>`" — named a row the ledger has no grammar for; there is no `for: funding:` word and none is needed.
keeping._keeping_mint: RETIRED 2026-09-14 (R12 superseded): no stake burns, so there is no σ leg and no keeping mint. AMENDED 2026-09-17: the rho base is the household's ALL-SOURCES mint before the close — primary and holo (the founder: "funding minted stamps contribute to the max stamps you can get from another fund. it compounds by design"). The 2026-09-14 line this replaces said "earned primary mint alone". The retired row's grammar stays lawful so a smuggled one parses and fails the close replay by name, and foldKeepingMint stays as the reader of the historical rows; the live ledger holds none.
keeping._exclusions: Self-stake exclusion is PAYER-SIDE and by HOUSEHOLD (2026-09-14, widened from handle): a payer's household's stakes are excluded from the mass that sizes that payer's mint. Sole-staker-sole-payer mints zero. There is no beneficiary carve-out — a beneficiary's stakes count like anyone else's for the other givers.
keeping._starforge_gives: RULED 2026-11-01 (Darko, 10:22, 10:27 and 10:36 EST): Starforge, the founder household, gives like any household, and what it would earn is kept PROVISIONAL, never minted. Verbatim, 10:22: "we should fill up the rest of the unfilled pots as the star forge household and then get stamps from that accordingly, because we want to make everything very fair and treat ourselves just like a household. From now on, so that we can continuously kind of push away the special unwritten authority that our household has held until now." And 10:36: "What if we just track the number of stamps that we should provisionally have minted for ourselves, but not actually mint them yet, just because I don't want to do that because there's no way to take it back. And we can just keep like this provisional number of like the effective stamps that we could currently kind of possess, but haven't actually minted." (1) Starforge's own dollars toward a posted need (it already pays the pots' bills directly; 10:27: "mark it and credit ourselves for filling the rest of the bill, which we do") are NOT pot-receipts and write nothing to the stamp ledger. They are recorded in WHITE_PAGES/starforge-provisional.json, with the holo the close would have minted them, computed by the arithmetic in § _what as if the dollars were a receipt from `wright` (its own household's stakes excluded per § _exclusions, clipped to the rho cap on its holdings). (2) Provisional stamps are a public record, not a balance: they move nothing, vote nothing and count in no ledger fold, gauge or weight, NOMOS's included. Minting any of them is a separate ruling. (3) The holo is credited to `wright` for now (10:27: "I think you should take the stamps, and we're soon going to restructure that so that stamps are shared throughout the household anyway"). (4) The treasury is unchanged: it may still cover a shortfall, minting nothing. (5) Every other household's close runs as before, and its mint is computed without Starforge's dollars. Any difference in how Starforge is treated, in either direction, is a NOMOS question (draft 2 § II.8).
keeping._intake_cap: D5 (Keemin, 2026-08-21): 'intake refuses dollars past a pot's posted target, mechanically (recording tool / door bounce), except pots explicitly marked uncapped.' A pot file carrying "uncapped": true is exempt (the Darko donation box is the standing case — a box with no target takes whatever arrives). Conversion's cap-at-1 on the funded fraction stays as the backstop: even if a dollar got past intake, it can never fund more than the posted need.
keeping._declared_not_exercised: Written 2026-08-20 on the seam/ledger-legs branch, encoding Keemin's rulings of that night; the matching math and the sigma leg's recipient were CORRECTED 2026-08-21 against the capture doc's section 8 after the first pass encoded a paraphrase, and the whole block was ALIGNED 2026-08-21 evening to that day's later rulings (R10 rho, R12 keeping mint, D1 ownership-as-read, D5 intake cap). No keeping row exists in the ledger; declaring the dial does not open a pot — opening one is the founder's word.
keeping._sigma: NO LEG IN THE KEEPING CLOSE since 2026-09-14 (there is no burn to split); LIVE FOR THE BOUNTY CONVERSION since 2026-09-15 as the deliverer's fraction of the staked mass (law_side.conversion, amended at the founder's word 'extend'). tools/epoch-close.mjs was rebuilt against the amended close under POS-33 (2026-09-17) and its close path reads no sigma at all; the conversion ceremony has no code yet (POS-12's open box).

conversion._: the bounty-conversion parameters, founder-ruled 2026-08-23 evening (fast defaults; the ceremony itself is POS-12's lane): a fulfilled bounty becomes the delivered mark, and standing stakes resolve by their mode. AMENDED 2026-09-15 at the founder's word ('extend' — the 2026-09-14 return rule covers every stake in town, the bounty conversion included, postmark#2811): no stake burns at a conversion; every standing stake returns whole; the mass they lent (M, the standing stakes at conversion, a fulfilled bounty being fully funded) sizes the fresh mint — the deliverer's wage and the author's carve, each household's own stakes excluded from the mass sized for it, rho-capped, the remainder un-minted. No conversion has ever run under either rule: the ledger carries none, and the only stake ever laid on a bounty was unstaked the same day (2026-08-17).
conversion._authors_carve: the idea lane's cut, amended 2026-09-15: the bounty's author is minted fresh floor(authors_carve x (1 - sigma) x M), liquid, source-tagged 'for: bounty:<mark> · carve', the author's own household's stakes excluded from M. Before the amendment this was a CARVE of the records issued from the burn ((1-sigma) x the pot-mode burn), never fresh issuance, the backers splitting the rest pro-rata by what they burned; nothing burns now, so the records leg is gone and the backers' return is their stamps home. Published on the menu before anyone stakes; ratified by accession.
conversion._ballot_auto_return: ballot-mode stakes return whole at completion AND in full on a withdrawn bounty; unstake stays free anytime. Nothing in ballot-mode ever burns — and since 2026-09-15 nothing in pot-mode does either; the modes differ by what the stakes DO (pot-mode sizes a reward; ballot-mode is a vote).
conversion._deliverer_paid: the labor lane, amended 2026-09-15: the deliverer is minted fresh floor(sigma x M), liquid — a wage, source-tagged 'for: bounty:<mark> · wage' (before: the deliverer's sigma share of the BURN re-minted liquid). The anti-laundering guard stands and is widened to the household, as the keeping close's was on 2026-09-14: the deliverer's household's stakes are excluded from the mass that sizes the wage — no household buys its own pay; sole-backer-sole-deliverer mints zero. rho caps it: no household receives more than rho x its earned base in one conversion. What remains of M after the wage and the carve is un-minted.

settlement._note: World-canon settles twice daily at the Worldkeeper's crossings (write-release ruling 8). Weights manifest at settlements; between crossings the record fluctuates and canon holds at the last blessed sha.
